newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan may ease restrictions on mainland tourists.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may ease restrictions on mainland tourists.

text.p: Taiwan is considering easing a ban on travel to the island for people living in rival mainland China, the China Times newspaper on Sunday quoted officials as saying.

Under proposals drafted by the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan would first allow in tour groups of employees of China's communist government agencies and state-owned companies, the paper said.
It would then allow limited visits by ordinary mainland residents with proof of adequate income or assets, it said.
The stage-by-stage opening would be aimed at preventing illegal over-stays by mainlanders who may threaten Taiwan's national security, the paper said.
The proposals, which require approval from the Mainland Affairs Council and the cabinet, did not give a specific timetable.
Taiwan in 1987 scrapped a decades-old ban on Taiwan residents visiting China, but visits by mainlanders to the island are still restricted.

Taiwan now allows visits by mainland professionals and businessmen. In 1996, more than 15 million Taiwanese traveled to the mainland while mainlanders visiting Taiwan totaled only 50,000, the paper said.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949. Beijing, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province, has since tried to push the island into international isolation.

A political thaw starting in the late 1980s promoted active exchanges between the two sides but relations have deteriorated since Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui made a private, but high-profile, visit to the United States in June 1995.
